clue.text: Among old people many found divine guidance

indicators.note: the word for many is placed among the letters of old plus people

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
L is the Roman numeral fifty, a conventional 'many'

explanation.surface: Amid a crowd of elderly folk, someone finds a message from the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: L (fifty, so 'many') goes among O and RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: At Delphi a priestess delivered prophecies from the god, so the shrine's pronouncement is guidance from heaven.

clue.text: Players training for short race

indicators.note: training reshapes the letters of short race into a new form

explanation.surface: Sportsmen getting into shape ahead of a sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of musicians who play together is a band.

clue.text: Animal running wild round Uganda's capital put in compound

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the next piece
running wild suggests the letters of animal scrambled
the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A beast loose around Uganda's main city is penned in an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running wild' gives ALMINA from ANIMAL; 'round' puts U from 'Uganda's capital' inside it. 'put in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aluminium oxide is a chemical compound.

clue.text: Ignited high explosive in limber

parts.note: lit means set alight

explanation.surface: Explosives set alight inside a gun carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: A limber is also a gun-carriage front, which suits the explosives; here it is the adjective meaning supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple and flexible in body, able to bend easily.

clue.text: Enthusiast gets on and flourishes

parts.note: a fan is a keen supporter
to fare is to get on, as in 'how are you faring?'

explanation.surface: A keen supporter makes progress and waves the flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourish of trumpets is a short ceremonial burst of brass, the same thing as a fanfare.

clue.text: A quiet pair is attracting joint training opportunity

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
someone who entices is attracting
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Two quiet people drawing in a shared opportunity to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: A period learning a trade under a skilled master is a placement for learning.

clue.text: Crude raft adrift and shattered

indicators.note: something adrift has come loose, so the letters of crude raft drift into a new order

explanation.surface: A roughly built raft floats away and breaks up.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken into pieces, like a cracked bone.

clue.text: Substitute husband

definitions.meaning: a stand-in player kept back for a team
as a verb, to keep back and conserve

explanation.surface: A stand-in spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare player waiting on the bench; to husband resources is to save them.

clue.text: Write letters in order to be charming

definitions.meaning: to give the letters of a word in their right sequence
as a noun, charming is the act of casting a magic charm

explanation.surface: Writing neatly is the way to win people over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' links the definitions; 'charming' is read as the noun, an enchantment.
explanation.definitionFit: To name a word's letters in order; a magic incantation is an enchantment.

clue.text: Crooked deal in which sucker loses royalty

definitions.text: Crooked deal in which sucker loses royalty

parts.words: Crooked deal in which sucker loses royalty
parts.note: a street con with three playing cards where the mark must find the queen and never does

explanation.surface: A rigged arrangement in which a fool sees the crown slip away.
explanation.walkthrough: Royalty is the queen card in the find-the-lady street swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A street swindle where punters bet on finding the queen among three face-down cards.

clue.text: Royal yacht, perhaps, in hot pursuit?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a vessel belonging to the royal court
the ardent wooing of a lover

explanation.surface: A monarch's yacht giving chase across the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the two definitions; the question mark flags the split reading as a court ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooing is an eager chase of a would-be partner; a ship of the royal court could be a state yacht.

clue.text: Lioness in retreat crossing one's path

indicators.note: the reversed name lies across the letter for one, holding it inside
retreating means going backwards, so the lioness's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Elsa is the famous lioness of the book and film Born Free
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A backing-off lioness strays across someone's way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns ELSA into ASLE, and 'crossing' puts I inside it; the 's of one's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage between rows of seats in a church or theatre is a walkway.

clue.text: Cut out pieces to make fo'c'sle, for example

definitions.text: Cut out pieces to make fo'c'sle, for example

parts.words: Cut out pieces to make fo'c'sle, for example
parts.note: forecastle loses letters, marked by apostrophes, when contracted to the sailor's spelling; the verb means to drop sounds that way

explanation.surface: Trimming a ship's word down to its nautical shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit a vowel or syllable in speech, as the apostrophes show in forecastle's short form.

clue.text: Sort of college that gets chosen by word of mouth

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in president-elect
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A college whose members are picked by spoken vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that gets' is link material between the definition and the pieces. The US electoral college picks the president.
explanation.definitionFit: The American body that formally chooses the president is called the Electoral College.

clue.text: Turner's use of light, now considered old-fashioned

definitions.text: Turner's use of light, now considered old-fashioned

parts.words: Turner's use of light, now considered old-fashioned
parts.note: not the painter's art but a car's arm that lit up when turning, a fitting long since outdated

explanation.surface: Critics now find the painter Turner's handling of light passé.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like J.M.W. Turner the painter; here a turner is a car turning, and the light is its old pop-out signal arm.
explanation.definitionFit: An old car signal arm that swung out and lit to show the driver was about to change direction.

clue.text: Right to vote outside a man's country

indicators.note: the country's name goes outside, holding the other piece

parts.note: France is a country
his means belonging to a man

explanation.surface: Being entitled to vote abroad in another man's homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffrage, the entitlement to take part in elections.

clue.text: Scoff at egghead going into the lead

indicators.note: the letter moves to the front, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: the head of egg is its first letter, E
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sneering at an intellectual who takes over the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' is not an intellectual but the head letter of egg, which goes before AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to gobble it down, a slang word for consuming.

clue.text: Examined poem in traditional form

indicators.note: the poem is placed inside the short form

parts.note: trad is the short form of traditional, as in trad jazz
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A poem was studied in its classical shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse a subject is to survey or go over it carefully.

clue.text: Port with sound distinctive character

indicators.note: the word sound tells us we want a word that is heard the same as another

parts.note: an air is a distinctive manner or character, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: A harbour town with its own special atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: AYR is a port on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish harbour town on the Firth of Clyde, so a place where ships dock.

clue.text: Complete over and attack verbally

parts.note: round means complete or whole, as in a round dozen
on can mean over or on top of

explanation.surface: Finishing an over in cricket, then rounding on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on someone suddenly with angry words.

clue.text: Word that has to be pronounced to get the spelling right

definitions.text: Word that has to be pronounced to get the spelling right

parts.words: Word that has to be pronounced to get the spelling right
parts.note: spelling here is casting a magic spell, which needs the conjuror's magic word said correctly

explanation.surface: A tip on pronunciation to help with spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' suggests orthography; it means working a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage magician's incantation, uttered to make a trick work.

clue.text: Bird with long legs making concerted breakaway?

definitions.text: Bird with long legs making concerted breakaway?

parts.words: Bird with long legs making concerted breakaway?
parts.note: a big long-legged game bird that, when alarmed, tends to run off over open ground rather than take wing

explanation.surface: A long-legged bird joins a mass escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A large heavy ground bird of open plains, known for running on strong long legs.

clue.text: Heads or tails?

parts.note: not a coin toss but what is chopped off: cutting off the top or end of something

explanation.surface: Someone calls as a coin spins.
explanation.walkthrough: The coin-toss call is a red herring; the verb shortens things by lopping their tops or ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten by removing the beginning or the end, as with heads or tails.

clue.text: Light sort of song

definitions.meaning: a portable lamp, the British word for a flashlight
a sentimental ballad of unrequited love

explanation.surface: A light little ditty.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-held lamp; a sad love ballad is called a torch song.

clue.text: Drop discrimination

definitions.meaning: a small sample to try, as in just a sip
refined judgment in matters of style

explanation.surface: Getting rid of prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount to try is a small sample; good judgment in style is refined discernment.

clue.text: On paper, this maneater is harmless

definitions.text: On paper, this maneater is harmless

parts.words: On paper, this maneater is harmless
parts.note: the phrase paper something means a threat that looks fierce but has no real power

explanation.surface: A man-eating cat looks harmless in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: On paper suggests 'in theory'; it points to the paper version of the big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped Asian big cat known to kill people; its paper version is an empty threat.

clue.text: They travel equal distances to different points on the Circle Line

definitions.text: They travel equal distances to different points on the Circle Line

parts.words: They travel equal distances to different points on the Circle Line
parts.note: lines from the centre of a circle all reach its edge at the same length

explanation.surface: Passengers on London's Circle Line Underground route ride equal stretches to various stops.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here it is simply a circle's circumference.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight lines from a circle's centre to its rim, all the same length.

clue.text: Fish product occupies vessel

parts.note: a thing that is in a place occupies it
a glass is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: Something made from fish fills a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatine got from the swim bladders of sturgeon and similar fish, used for clarifying wine.

clue.text: Layer picks nags

parts.note: a hen is a bird that lays eggs
to peck is to pick at with the beak

explanation.surface: A bird picks at old horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantly scolding someone, especially a husband, is browbeating them.

clue.text: Involved in traffic, darted out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of darted being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in the cars dashed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic means commerce, so one who dealt in goods has done business.
